md_description: This DAG represents freshwater lake water sampling across depths, locations, and seasons, followed by direct environmental measurements and metagenomic sequencing of extracted nucleic acids. It captures the generation of environmental readings, raw sequencing data, and computed metagenomic profiles used to analyze microbial community structure, function, and responses to changing aquatic conditions.

freshwater_lake_water_samples.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the intrinsic identity and provenance of the collected water samples, not the sampling process or downstream measurements. I included fields for sample identity, lake/source provenance, collection depth, geographic location, season, and basic sample nature because those are properties of the samples themselves and are needed to distinguish samples across the workflow. I excluded capture settings, environmental readings, extraction/library/sequencing details, and any file or computed outputs because those belong to downstream Capture, Process, Signal, or Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no prior naming conflicts to avoid. I also avoided experiment-wide identifiers unless they are inherent to individual sample records, and I kept the schema flat for this node only.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the individual freshwater lake water sample record. Use a stable string format such as 'FLAKE-001' or 'siteA_depth5m_spring'. Assigned at collection and used to link this sample to environmental measurements, nucleic acid extraction, and sequencing outputs downstream.

Name of the freshwater lake from which the water sample was collected, as recorded at sampling. Example: 'Lake Superior' or a project-specific site name. Captures the source water body for provenance.

Depth below the water surface at which the sample was collected, measured at sampling in meters. Typical freshwater sampling depths may range from 0 to tens of meters, depending on lake depth and study design.

Sampling location within the lake or lake system, recorded as a site label, station name, coordinate string, or equivalent location descriptor at collection time. Example: 'north basin', 'station_3', or '45.123N_93.456W'.
Season when the sample was collected, as a coarse temporal descriptor of sampling context. Use one of the allowed values to distinguish recurring seasonal campaigns.
Physical sample type represented by this record. For this DAG it should be freshwater lake water collected for environmental and metagenomic analysis.
Date the water sample was collected in local calendar date format. Record the actual sampling date when the sample was taken, if available, to support temporal grouping across seasons.

Immediate post-collection storage condition of the water sample before downstream processing, describing how the collected material was kept as an entity property. Example values are constrained to common preservation states used for aquatic samples.

environmental_measurements_capture.reasoning: This Capture node should describe the measurement session and instrument configuration used to record environmental parameters from the water sample. I included the measured parameter set, the platform/instrument identity, and key operational settings relevant to how readings were acquired. I excluded sample provenance fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded raw measurement outputs and file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided repeating any root identifiers or sample descriptors, and I did not include downstream interpretation of the measurements because that belongs to later analysis nodes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the environmental measurement session or event, used to link the capture to the corresponding water sample and downstream environmental readings. Example format: 'ENVCAP-0001'.
Date on which the environmental parameters were measured from the collected water sample. Record the actual capture date, typically the same day as collection or immediately after sample acquisition.
Manufacturer of the field sensor or laboratory analyzer used to measure the environmental parameters. Record the hardware vendor responsible for the measurement device used in this capture session.
Model name or number of the measurement instrument used for the environmental capture session. Example: a specific dissolved oxygen meter, multiparameter sonde, or nutrient analyzer model.

Serial number of the instrument used for environmental measurement, recorded to identify the exact hardware instance employed in this capture session. Use the serial string printed by the manufacturer.

Set of environmental parameters actively measured during this capture session from the water sample. Include only the parameters directly acquired here, such as temperature, dissolved oxygen, and nutrient concentrations.
Operational mode used for the environmental measurement session, describing whether readings were obtained in situ or from a collected sample in the lab.
Whether the instrument was calibrated before this measurement session, as recorded at the time of capture. This is a quality-control setting of the capture operation, not the scientific result.

Number of replicate readings acquired for the environmental measurement session for the sample, if multiple technical readings were taken to improve reliability. Typical values are positive integers such as 1, 2, or 3.

environmental_parameter_signal.reasoning: This Signal node should describe the raw measurement artefact produced by the capture step: the technical form of the environmental readings, their size/structure, storage, and basic quality flags. I included file-oriented and data-structure fields because those belong to raw signal identity, not to the capture instrument or sample provenance. I excluded the actual parameter values and measurement settings because those are represented by the upstream Capture node, and I excluded downstream interpretation because that belongs to derivative analysis nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw environmental measurement file or exported record produced by the capture session. Example: 'env_readings_sample001.csv'. This identifies the raw data artefact for the lake sample.
File format of the raw environmental measurement artefact as stored or exported from the capture system. Use the format actually received for dataset archiving.
Size of the raw environmental measurement file in bytes, measured after capture and before any downstream processing. Useful for validating completeness and storage footprint.
Number of raw measurement records or rows in the environmental parameter signal file. For a single sample this may be one record, while instrument exports can contain multiple time-stamped rows.

Labels for the data dimensions present in the raw environmental signal, such as time, parameter name, and replicate channel. Provide the structural organization of the raw artefact rather than the scientific values.
Relative or absolute storage path or URI where the raw environmental measurement file is kept. Example: '/data/env/sample001.csv' or an object-store URI.
Basic quality flag assigned to the raw environmental measurement artefact at ingestion or export time. Indicates whether the file appears usable before downstream analysis.

nucleic_acid_extraction.reasoning: This Process node should describe how nucleic acids were extracted from the water sample, including protocol details, reagents, conditions, operator/software agent, and a process-level quality indicator. I included extraction chemistry and operational parameters because those define the transformation performed on the sample. I excluded sample provenance fields because they belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded properties of the extracted nucleic acids themselves because those belong to the downstream Entity node. I also avoided any sequencing or library-preparation fields because those are downstream processes in the DAG. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no naming conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Name of the nucleic acid extraction protocol or kit used to process the freshwater water sample. Example: a commercial kit name or in-house protocol label used at the time of extraction.
Version or revision of the extraction protocol, kit, or SOP applied during nucleic acid extraction. Record the exact version used so the process can be reproduced.
Primary reagent kit or extraction chemistry used to isolate microbial nucleic acids from the water sample. Record the kit or chemistry identifier used in this process step.
Volume of lake water input to the extraction process, measured in milliliters at the start of extraction. Typical values depend on study design and filtration/extraction workflow.
General extraction method category used for the process, describing the physical or chemical approach applied to recover nucleic acids from the water sample.

Temperature at which the extraction reaction or incubation step was performed, measured in degrees Celsius during the process. Typical laboratory extraction temperatures may range from cold handling to elevated incubation conditions.
Duration of the main extraction incubation or lysis step, measured in minutes during the process. Record the elapsed time used to recover nucleic acids from the sample.
Identifier for the researcher or technician who performed the extraction, recorded as a stable string such as a staff ID or initials. This is the human agent carrying out the process.

Overall process-level quality indicator for the extraction outcome, recorded after the extraction step and before library preparation. Use a coarse flag to indicate whether the nucleic acid recovery was acceptable for downstream sequencing.

extracted_nucleic_acids.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the intrinsic properties and provenance of the recovered nucleic acid material, not the extraction process or later library/sequencing steps. I included identity, material type, concentration, volume, purity, integrity, and storage because these are properties of the extracted nucleic acids themselves and are needed for downstream handling and reproducibility. I excluded extraction protocol parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded library-preparation inputs or sequencing outputs because they belong downstream. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no overlaps to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the extracted nucleic acid material derived from a water sample. Example format: 'ENA-0001' or a lab inventory barcode. Use this string to track the purified material into library preparation.
Type of nucleic acid recovered from the extraction step. Record whether the material is DNA, RNA, or a mixed DNA/RNA extract as present in the purified entity.

Measured concentration of the purified nucleic acid extract, reported in ng/µL. Record the concentration as measured after extraction and before library preparation. Typical values may range from low to high depending on sample biomass and extraction efficiency.
Total volume of the purified nucleic acid extract available for downstream library preparation, reported in microliters. Measure this after extraction and cleanup.
Spectrophotometric purity ratio A260/A280 of the extracted nucleic acid material, measured after purification to assess contamination by protein or other absorbent impurities.

Quality measure describing the integrity of the extracted nucleic acid material at the point it is handed off for library preparation. This may be a lab-specific integrity score, such as a RNA integrity or DNA integrity metric.

Storage condition of the extracted nucleic acids before library preparation, recorded as the preservation state of the material entity. Example values indicate whether the extract was kept frozen or refrigerated.

Storage temperature of the extracted nucleic acids after purification and before library preparation, reported in degrees Celsius. Typical values may include freezer or cold-room storage temperatures.

library_preparation.reasoning: This Process node should describe how purified nucleic acids were converted into a sequencing-ready library, including library-prep protocol details, adapter/insert configuration, amplification conditions, and process-level quality. I included workflow and reagent settings because those define the transformation performed on the extracted nucleic acids. I excluded properties of the input extract and properties of the final library itself because those belong to the upstream and downstream Entity nodes, respectively. I also excluded sequencing instrument details and raw read outputs because those belong to the later Capture and Signal nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Name of the library preparation protocol or kit used to convert extracted nucleic acids into a sequencing-ready library. Example: a commercial metagenomic library kit label or in-house protocol name.
Version or revision of the library preparation protocol, kit, or SOP applied in this process step. Record the exact version used for reproducibility.

Amount of extracted nucleic acid input used for library preparation, reported in ng at the start of the process. Typical library prep inputs may range from picogram to nanogram quantities depending on the kit and sample quality.
Adapter chemistry or adapter category used during library construction. Record the adapter type used to make the fragments sequencing-ready.
Approximate target insert size of the library fragments, measured or specified in base pairs during library preparation. This describes the fragment length distribution intended for sequencing.
Number of PCR amplification cycles used during library preparation, if amplification was performed. Record the exact cycle count applied to the library construction workflow.
Method used to select fragment sizes during library preparation, if applicable. This describes how the library was enriched for the desired fragment length range.
Identifier for the researcher or technician who performed the library preparation, recorded as a stable string such as a staff ID or initials.
Overall quality indicator for the library preparation outcome, recorded after preparation and before sequencing. Use a coarse flag indicating whether the library is suitable for sequencing.

metagenomic_library.reasoning: This Entity node should capture the intrinsic identity and physical properties of the sequencing-ready library produced by library preparation, not the preparation protocol itself or the sequencing run. I included identifiers, library type, fragment size, concentration, molarity, and storage because these are properties of the library material that downstream sequencing will consume. I excluded kit/reagent and amplification settings because those belong to the library preparation Process node, and I excluded sequencing instrument/run settings because those belong to the Capture node. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no duplicate field names to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the sequencing-ready metagenomic library derived from the extracted environmental nucleic acids. Example format: 'MGLIB-0001' or a library barcode used to track the material into sequencing.
Molecular content of the sequencing-ready library material. Record whether the library is derived from DNA, RNA, or a mixed nucleic acid input.
Approximate fragment size or insert length of the final sequencing-ready library, reported in base pairs. Measure or estimate this after library preparation and before sequencing.
Concentration of the sequencing-ready library, reported in ng/µL at the time it is handed off to sequencing. Typical values depend on library type and assay sensitivity.
Molar concentration of the sequencing-ready library, reported in nM and measured before sequencing loading. This is commonly used to normalize libraries for sequencing.
Method used to quantify the final library material before sequencing, such as fluorometric or qPCR-based quantification. Record the assay category used for the entity measurement.
Storage condition of the sequencing-ready library before it is loaded onto the sequencer. Record how the library material was kept after preparation and before capture.
Barcode or tube label associated with the sequencing-ready library entity, if a separate inventory code is used. Example: a lab barcode string linking physical aliquots to records.

metagenomic_sequencing_capture.reasoning: This Capture node should describe the sequencing session and instrument configuration used to generate raw metagenomic reads from the library. I included sequencer identity, run configuration, flow cell/run settings, and loading parameters because those are actively controlled capture properties. I excluded library material properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded file format, read counts, and quality metrics because those belong to the downstream raw Signal node. I also avoided software-pipeline details because sequencing capture is hardware-centric in this DAG. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no naming conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the sequencing run or capture session that produced the raw metagenomic reads. Example format: 'SEQRUN-0001'. Use this to link the library to the specific instrument session.
Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the metagenomic capture session. Record the hardware vendor responsible for the sequencer.
Model name or number of the sequencing instrument used to generate raw reads. Example: a specific benchtop or high-throughput sequencer model.
Serial number of the sequencing instrument used in this capture session, recorded to identify the exact hardware instance employed.
Sequencing chemistry or reagent kit version used during the capture session. Record the chemistry family or kit designation applied to the run.
Nominal read length programmed for the sequencing run, reported in base pairs. Typical values are the intended read length for each sequencing direction or read mode.
Sequencing run configuration used for the capture session, describing the read structure acquired by the instrument.
Flow cell or consumable type used in the sequencing session, if applicable to the instrument platform. Record the specific consumable format loaded for capture.
Concentration of the metagenomic library loaded onto the sequencer for this capture session, reported in nM. This is an actively controlled instrument loading parameter.

Overall quality indicator for the sequencing capture session, recorded at the end of the run before downstream file processing. Use a coarse flag to indicate whether the run produced usable raw reads.

raw_metagenomic_reads.reasoning: This Signal node should describe the raw sequencing artefact itself: its file identity, format, size, read structure, technical yield, and storage location. I included file-level and run-output characteristics because those define the raw data object generated by sequencing. I excluded sequencing instrument settings and loading parameters because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded trimming, filtering, or interpretive metrics because those belong to downstream Process or Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no duplicate field names to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw metagenomic sequencing file produced by the sequencing run. Example: 'sample001_R1.fastq.gz' or a paired-file set name. This identifies the raw read artefact.
File format of the raw sequencing reads as stored or delivered from the sequencer. Use the actual format received for archiving and analysis.
Size of the raw read file in bytes, measured after sequencing and before any downstream processing. Use this to assess storage footprint and file completeness.
Total number of raw sequencing reads contained in the file or file pair generated by the run. Record the technical output count before filtering or trimming.
Total number of bases represented across the raw sequencing reads, reported in base pairs. This is a signal-level summary of sequence yield before processing.
Average base-call quality score for the raw reads, calculated at the file level before downstream filtering. Record the aggregate technical quality of the raw sequencing artefact.
Whether the raw sequencing data contain one or two read files per library molecule. Use this to describe the raw read structure delivered by the sequencer.
Relative or absolute path or URI where the raw metagenomic read file is stored. Example: '/data/seq/sample001.fastq.gz' or an object-store URI.

read_processing.reasoning: This Process node should describe how raw reads were filtered and prepared, including software/pipeline agent details, trimming and filtering parameters, and process-level output quality. I included the processing workflow and key thresholds because those define the transformation from raw reads to processed reads. I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the properties of the processed read artefact itself because those belong to the downstream Signal node. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no naming conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Name of the bioinformatics pipeline or workflow used to process raw metagenomic reads. Example: a specific quality-control and filtering pipeline label used for this dataset.
Version or release of the read-processing pipeline or workflow applied to the raw reads. Record the exact version used so results can be reproduced.
Minimum Phred quality threshold used to trim or discard low-quality bases or reads during processing. Typical values are integers such as 20 or 30.
Minimum allowed read length after trimming/filtering, reported in base pairs. Reads shorter than this threshold are removed or excluded from downstream profiling.
Whether contaminant filtering was applied during read processing. Use this to indicate if non-target sequences were removed before metagenomic profiling.
Whether adapter trimming was enabled as part of the read processing workflow. This describes a preprocessing operation applied to raw reads.
Whether duplicate reads were removed during processing. Use this to indicate if the pipeline collapsed or excluded redundant reads before profiling.
Identifier for the analyst, researcher, or automated workflow owner responsible for executing the read-processing step. Record a stable string such as a staff ID or pipeline owner label.

Overall quality indicator for the processed-read output of this processing step, recorded after filtering and before downstream profiling. Use a coarse flag indicating suitability for metagenomic analysis.

processed_metagenomic_reads.reasoning: This Signal node should describe the processed read artefact itself: the technical file identity, size, read counts, retention statistics, and storage location after filtering/trimming. I included post-processing quality and yield metrics because those are properties of the resulting signal, not the processing steps. I excluded pipeline names, trimming thresholds, and software parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node. I also excluded downstream taxonomic or functional interpretations because those belong to the metagenomic profile Derivative node. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no naming conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Name of the processed metagenomic read file produced after quality trimming and filtering. Example: 'sample001_trimmed.fastq.gz'.
File format of the processed reads after read processing. Use the actual stored format delivered to downstream profiling.
Size of the processed read file in bytes after filtering and trimming. Record this after the read-processing step and before downstream profiling.
Number of reads remaining after quality trimming and filtering. This is the surviving read count available for metagenomic profiling.
Total number of bases represented by the processed reads, reported in base pairs after filtering and trimming. This summarizes the usable sequence yield for profiling.
Fraction of raw reads retained after read processing, calculated as processed reads divided by raw reads. This is a technical yield metric for the processed signal.
Average base-call quality score across the processed reads after trimming and filtering. Use this to summarize the technical quality of the post-processed signal.
Relative or absolute path or URI where the processed read file is stored. Example: '/data/processed/sample001_trimmed.fastq.gz' or an object-store URI.

metagenomic_profiling.reasoning: This Process node should describe how processed reads were analyzed to infer community structure and function, including the analysis workflow, reference resources, parameters, and process-level output quality. I included algorithmic and database settings because those define the transformation from processed reads to a computed profile. I excluded properties of the processed reads themselves because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the computed profile fields because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Name of the metagenomic profiling pipeline or workflow used to analyze processed reads. Example: a taxonomic and functional profiling pipeline label used for this dataset.
Version or release of the profiling pipeline applied to the processed reads. Record the exact software or workflow version used for reproducibility.
Name of the reference database used during metagenomic profiling, such as a taxonomic, functional, or marker-gene database. This identifies the knowledge base used for inference.
Version or release date of the reference database used for profiling. Record the exact database version to support reproducible classification and annotation.
General method used to infer microbial community structure and functional composition from the processed reads. This describes the analytical strategy applied in the process.
Minimum confidence threshold applied when assigning taxonomic or functional features during profiling. Record the cutoff used by the analysis pipeline, typically as a probability or score threshold.

Minimum alignment identity or similarity threshold used by the profiling process, if applicable. Record the cutoff applied when mapping reads to references, typically expressed as a fraction or percentage.
Identifier for the analyst, researcher, or automated workflow owner responsible for running the metagenomic profiling step. Record a stable string such as a staff ID or pipeline owner label.

Overall quality indicator for the profiling process output, recorded after analysis and before interpretation. Use a coarse flag indicating whether the profiling run produced suitable results for downstream integration.

metagenomic_profile.reasoning: This Derivative node should describe the computed metagenomic result itself: the profile type, dimensions, feature space, summary statistics, and scientific quality indicators. I included output structure and interpretation-ready summary fields because those belong to the derived profile artifact. I excluded profiling algorithm settings, databases, and thresholds because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded raw or processed read properties because those belong to Signal nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no naming conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed metagenomic profile derived from a processed read set. Example format: 'MPROF-0001'. Use this to link the derivative result to the corresponding sample and profiling run.
Type of computed profile represented by this derivative. Indicate whether the output is taxonomic, functional, or a combined profile.
Lowest taxonomic rank represented in the computed profile, if taxonomic results are included. Record the finest level at which features are reported, such as genus or species.
Number of distinct taxonomic or functional features reported in the computed profile. This is a derivative output dimension measured after analysis.
Method used to normalize feature abundances in the computed profile, such as relative abundance or count normalization. Record the representation applied to make profiles comparable across samples.
Summary diversity metric computed from the profile for the sample, if included in this derivative. Record the specific diversity statistic used to summarize within-sample community diversity.
Fraction or percentage of reads/features assigned to functional categories in the computed profile. This is a scientific quality indicator for the derivative output.
Relative or absolute path or URI where the computed metagenomic profile is stored. Example: '/data/profiles/sample001_profile.tsv' or an object-store URI.

Overall quality indicator for the computed profile, recorded after metagenomic profiling and before integrated environmental analysis. Use a coarse flag to indicate whether the derivative is suitable for downstream integration and interpretation.

integrative_environmental_analysis.reasoning: This Process node should describe the integrative analysis that combines environmental measurements and metagenomic profiles, so I included analysis method, software/pipeline identity and version, statistical design, covariates, and output quality indicators. These are the operational details of how the integration was performed. I excluded environmental reading values, sampling provenance, and profile contents because those belong to upstream Entity/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also excluded the integrated result itself because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Name of the integrative statistical or computational analysis workflow used to combine environmental measurements with metagenomic profiles. Example: a multivariate association analysis or ecological response modeling pipeline label.
Version or revision of the integrative analysis workflow, script, or software package used for the analysis. Record the exact version to support reproducibility.
General model or statistical approach used for the integrative analysis of environmental and microbial data. This describes the analytical strategy applied to study community response.

Environmental or ecological response variables included as targets in the integrative analysis, such as temperature, dissolved oxygen, nutrient concentration, depth, location, or season. Record the variable names used in the model.

Set of predictor covariates included in the integrative analysis, such as sampling depth, geographic location, season, and environmental chemistry. Record the covariate group used to explain microbial response.
Method used to adjust for multiple statistical tests in the integrative analysis, if applicable. Record the correction strategy used to control false positives.
Threshold used to determine statistically significant associations or effects in the integrative analysis, typically expressed as a p-value or adjusted p-value cutoff.
Identifier for the researcher, analyst, or automated workflow owner responsible for running the integrative environmental analysis. Record a stable string such as a staff ID or pipeline owner label.

Overall quality indicator for the integrative analysis output, recorded after modeling and before reporting. Use a coarse flag to indicate whether the analysis was successful and suitable for interpretation.

response_analysis_result.reasoning: This Derivative node should describe the integrated analytical output itself, not the statistical workflow that produced it. I included result identity, result type, effect/association summaries, significance summaries, explained variance, and output storage because these characterize the computed response-analysis artefact. I excluded environmental measurement values, metagenomic profile content, and model settings because those belong to upstream nodes, especially the integrative analysis Process node. I also avoided repeating sample identifiers or experiment-level identifiers that were already assigned at the root and should not be duplicated here. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no naming conflicts to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the integrated response analysis result. Example format: 'RESP-0001'. Use this to link the derivative output to the specific integration analysis run.
Type of integrated analytical output produced by the response analysis. Record the broad output category represented by this derivative.

Primary summary metric describing the strength or direction of the microbial response to environmental variables in the integrated result. Use the specific numeric summary reported by the analysis, such as an effect size or correlation coefficient.
Number of microbial features or associations deemed significant in the integrated response analysis after statistical testing and correction. Record the count produced by the derivative output.

Fraction of variance in microbial community structure or function explained by the integrated environmental analysis, reported as a proportion between 0 and 1 or equivalent percentage. This is a key scientific quality indicator for the derived result.

Environmental variables represented in the integrated response result, such as temperature, dissolved oxygen, nutrient concentration, depth, location, and season. Record the variables summarized by the derivative output.
Overall significance or interpretability flag for the integrated response result, indicating whether the derivative output contains supported associations or responses suitable for reporting.
Relative or absolute path or URI where the integrated response analysis result is stored. Example: '/data/results/response_analysis_summary.csv' or an object-store URI.
